papers.title_en: A Lightweight Velocity Correction Framework for Improving Instruction Following in Few-Step Text-to-Image Generation
papers.authors: Yating Gao, Zhenlong Zhu, Wen Zihao, Lenan Zhang, Jiexiong Wang, Yang Yang, Guanjun Jiang, Yixiong Zou, Takuya Maekawa
papers.evidence: 提升少步文本到图像生成的指令遵循能力
papers.tldr: 少步文本到图像生成器虽能用极少前向次数产出高质量图像，但在多主体、交互、空间关系、计数和属性绑定等复杂提示上常出错。本文提出轻量速度修正框架，冻结6B参数生成器，仅训练不到20M参数的修正器，在选定采样步上学习速度残差调整。借助On-Trajectory Flow-Bridge监督，在修正后实际到达的状态上生成残差目标。在复杂场景分布上，成对指令遵循评估相对冻结Z-Image-Turbo取得+17.60个百分点净胜，单图端到端延迟仅增加26.9毫秒（0.84%），且不增加骨干网络评估次数。
papers.abstract_en: Few-step text-to-image generators produce high-quality images with few network forward passes, yet struggle with complex prompts involving multiple subjects, interactions, spatial relations, counting, and attribute binding. Can these errors be reduced without changing the generator's parameters or increasing its forward-pass count? We propose a lightweight correction framework for a frozen 6B-parameter generator. The generator predicts velocities that determine how its intermediate image representation is updated; a corrector with fewer than 20M parameters learns residual adjustments at selected sampling steps. Because earlier corrections change the states encountered at later steps, our On-Trajectory Flow-Bridge Supervision derives residual targets at the states actually reached during corrected generation. A single corrector is shared across selected steps and runs in parallel with the generator. Only the corrector is trained, requiring neither reward optimization nor re-distillation. To our knowledge, this is the first framework for lightweight velocity-residual adaptation of fully frozen few-step text-to-image generators that preserves their original sampling schedule and forward-pass count. On our target complex-scene distribution, the framework achieves a +17.60-percentage-point NetWin over frozen Z-Image-Turbo in pairwise instruction-following evaluation, with only 26.9 ms (0.84%) additional end-to-end latency per image and no increase in backbone evaluations.

papers.title_en: Images Talk Back: Guiding MMDiTs by Suppressing Image-to-Text Feedback
papers.authors: Yucheng Yang, Xiaoxiao Sun, Shusheng Yang, Jiakang Chen, Serena Yeung-Levy
papers.evidence: 通过抑制图到文反馈引导文生图扩散Transformer
papers.tldr: 多模态扩散Transformer中，演化图像经联合注意力改写文本表征并反哺图像更新，可能固化已有错误。为此提出语义反馈引导SFG，通过远离增强图文反馈的辅助分支来抑制图像到文本反馈，并加强文本到图像条件；原地版iSFG无需额外模型评估。在FLUX上，SFG与CFG结合将GenEval从0.6661升至0.7479；SD3.5M上iSFG以零额外NFE取得+1.33 HPSv2.1。该控制还可迁移至视频生成，提升VBench。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiTs) allow the evolving image to update internal text representations through joint attention. These representations then guide subsequent image updates, raising a question: does this feedback help correct deviations from the prompt, or preserve them? We find that image-to-text (I2T) feedback can preserve the objects and attributes already represented in the evolving image, including errors. Transplanting I2T messages can rescue failures or disrupt successes. At matched intervention strengths, suppressing the influence of I2T feedback improves generation, whereas opposite controls degrade it. These findings motivate Semantic Feedback Guidance (SFG), which suppresses the influence of I2T feedback by guiding away from an auxiliary branch that strengthens this feedback and weakens text-to-image conditioning. The in-place variant, iSFG, directly suppresses I2T feedback and strengthens text-to-image conditioning, requiring no extra model evaluations. Temporal interventions motivate running the SFG branch during the first 20% of image sampling steps, requiring about $1.2\times$ the base NFE without classifier-free guidance (CFG). Experiments across three image-generation backbones show gains in alignment and preference-model scores. On FLUX, adding SFG to CFG raises GenEval from $0.6661$ to $0.7479$; on SD3.5M, iSFG adds $+1.33$ HPSv2.1 over CFG at zero extra NFE. The control also transfers to text-to-video and image-to-video generation, improving VBench scores. Code is available at https://github.com/yyc1215lll-creator/SFG.

papers.title_en: ThinkDrag: Semantic Drag-Based Image Editing with Visual Reasoning
papers.authors: Armando Fortes, Tianyi Wei, Chindanai Trakantannarong, Shangchen Zhou, Xingang Pan
papers.evidence: 带视觉推理的拖拽式可控图像编辑
papers.tldr: 现有拖拽式图像编辑多把拖拽视为几何位移，难以从稀疏点约束推断语义变换。ThinkDrag 提出统一多模态框架，结合视觉推理，将点约束关联到物体与场景级语义编辑，并可生成显式推理轨迹。方法还引入 Drag Endpoint Markers 提供图像空间对应信号，并构建语义拖拽数据集与 DragBench++ 基准。实验显示其生成质量与合理性达 SOTA，同时保持有竞争力的点跟随精度。
papers.abstract_en: Drag-based image editing provides an intuitive interface for spatially controlled image manipulation by allowing users to specify handle and target points. Existing methods have made substantial progress through optimization-based, one-step, and feed-forward formulations, but they often interpret drag instructions as geometric displacements. This limits their effectiveness when the desired edit depends on interpreting image content and inferring a plausible semantic transformation from sparse point constraints. We introduce ThinkDrag, a unified multimodal framework for drag-based image editing with visual reasoning. ThinkDrag is trained to associate point constraints with meaningful object- and scene-level transformations, and can optionally produce an explicit reasoning trace that interprets the intended edit before image generation. This reasoning trace improves interpretability, particularly for ambiguous drags. Drag Endpoint Markers, motivated by an analysis of cross-image attention, provide an explicit correspondence signal that grounds each drag in image space. To support this framework, we construct a supervised dataset of semantic drag transformations paired with reasoning traces and introduce DragBench++, a benchmark targeting challenging drag-based editing scenarios with reference edit solutions. Experiments show that ThinkDrag achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving generation quality and plausibility while maintaining competitive point-following precision.

papers.title_en: Exploring Attention Sinks in Text-to-Image Transformers from Diffusion and Autoregressive Models
papers.authors: Binglei Li, Mengping Yang, Zhiyu Tan, Wenxu Qian, Junping Zhang, Hao Li
papers.evidence: 扩散与自回归文生图Transformer中的注意力汇聚
papers.tldr: 注意力汇在LLM中被广泛研究，但在文生图Transformer中尚不清楚。本文系统分析双向扩散与因果自回归T2I模型，定位注意力汇并干预验证其功能。发现两类架构均存在汇，但模式不同且随阶段、层、头变化；扰动汇相关头影响更大，register token可重分配并保持性能。为T2I注意力机制分析与设计提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Attention sinks are tokens or positions that consistently receive disproportionate attention mass, often beyond what their semantic content would suggest. Despite extensive study in large language models, their behavior and functional relevance in text-to-image (T2I) Transformers remain largely unexplored. To fill this gap and better understand how text-to-image Transformers allocate and route attention, we explore this phenomenon of text-to-image transformers across bidirectional diffusion models and causal autoregressive models. Specifically, we explore whether attention sinks exist, where they emerge, and how they functionally influence generation. Through systematic attention analysis and targeted interventions, we identify that attention sinks emerge in both bidirectional diffusion and autoregressive models but exhibit distinct patterns. The autoregressive model concentrates attention on the first and global-scale tokens, whereas the bidirectional models develop sinks near modality boundaries, within text regions, and at spatial corners. Moreover, these patterns vary across generation stages and are localized to a sparse subset of layers and heads. To assess their functional relevance, we perturb sink-related heads and token positions. It turns out that perturbing sink-ranked heads produces larger average changes than non-sink comparisons, while some sink-position perturbations have limited effects on bidirectional model scores. We further introduce register tokens to redistribute attention sinks and find that several configurations preserve or modestly improve generation performance. Overall, attention sinks are architecture-, inference-stage-, and component-dependent phenomena, providing a basis for mechanistic analysis and principled attention design in text-to-image transformers.

papers.title_en: Stride: Scale-Aware Multi-Agent Evolutionary Refinement for Infographic Generation
papers.evidence: 在冻结文生图生成器上进行约束驱动精炼
papers.tldr: 信息图生成需同时满足大量视觉、文本与语义约束，现有基于多模态验证器的迭代式智能体精修存在尺度错配：局部编辑难改全局构图，整图重生成又易破坏正确区域。Stride将精修建模为历史感知的进化策略，分离约束评估与视觉定位，并把全局修改路由给composer、局部修正交给retoucher；每个子智能体内部规划并生成多候选，仅在验证器分数提升时接受。采用全开放权重生成-验证系统，Stride在BizGenEval超越Nano-Banana-2.0与Seedream-5.0-Pro，在IGenBench匹配GPT-Image-2.0并超越Seedream-5.0-Pro，在WISE取得新SOTA，且显著优于现有智能体方法。
papers.abstract_en: Infographic generation challenges text-to-image models because a single image must satisfy numerous visual, textual, and semantic constraints. Iterative agentic refinement with a multimodal verifier is a natural remedy, but existing methods face a scale mismatch: local edits cannot correct global composition errors, while full regeneration may destroy already-correct regions. We introduce Stride, a constraint-grounded multi-agent framework that treats refinement over any frozen generator as a history-aware evolution strategy. Stride separates constraint evaluation - whether each requirement is satisfied - from visual grounding - where and how it is violated. It then routes global revisions to a composer subagent and local corrections to a retoucher subagent. Each subagent conducts internal planning and generates multiple candidates, while Stride accepts a candidate only when it improves the verifier score, reducing regression across iterations. Because stochastic generators and imperfect verifiers make any single step unreliable, it is this combination of scale-aware routing, per-step redundancy, and monotonic acceptance that yields stable improvement across iterations. With fully open-weight generator-verifier systems, Stride outperforms proprietary systems including Nano-Banana-2.0 and Seedream-5.0-Pro on BizGenEval, matches GPT-Image-2.0 and surpasses Seedream-5.0-Pro on IGenBench, and achieves a new state-of-the-art score on WISE, while substantially outperforming existing agentic methods across all evaluated benchmarks.

papers.title_en: InstantFusion: A Shared Latent Interface for Heterogeneous Image Generators
papers.authors: Xuanlang Dai, Jiazi Bu, Yujie Zhou, Yuhong Liu, Beichen Zhang, Penghui Yang, Ziyu Liu, Yuhang Zang
papers.evidence: 面向异构扩散图像生成器的共享潜在接口
papers.tldr: 扩散/流生成器架构日益异构，跨模型隐空间对齐与去噪动态一致性仍待探索。作者发现独立模型的隐空间组织相似，直接交接中间状态可保留粗粒度内容。为此提出InstantFusion：用模型专属LAE把中间状态投影到共享隐空间，再解码至目标生成器，并用同图同噪声对齐和局部去噪速度同步训练。该接口无需逐对映射即可衔接冻结生成器，在加速、多偏好组合、跨架构在线蒸馏与跨模型组合中表现有竞争力。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion/flow models have emerged as the de facto paradigms for image generation, giving rise to a diverse family of modern generators with increasingly heterogeneous architectures and representations. Despite their remarkable generation capabilities, the cross-model alignment of latent representations and the consistency of their underlying denoising dynamics remain underexplored. In this work, we uncover an intriguing cross-model compatibility: independently trained generators exhibit similar latent spatial organization, while directly handing off intermediate states between unaligned models can still preserve coarse visual content. Motivated by these observations, we propose InstantFusion, a lightweight shared latent interface that connects the denoising trajectories of heterogeneous image generators. Specifically, to enable flexible cross-model state translation, model-specific Latent AutoEncoders (LAEs) are introduced to project intermediate states from different generators into a shared latent space and decode them into the latent space of a target generator. This shared space is constrained by two complementary objectives: aligning intermediate states derived from the same image at matched noise levels and synchronizing their corresponding local denoising velocities. Once trained, InstantFusion allows denoising to seamlessly transition across frozen generators without requiring a dedicated mapping for every model pair. The versatility of InstantFusion is demonstrated across acceleration, multi-preference composition, cross-architecture on-policy distillation, and cross-model composition, achieving competitive performance across these diverse settings.

papers.title_en: Equal Path Cost, Unequal Output Effects: Understanding Perturbation Propagation in Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Wei Guo, Yaowen Zhang, Xingtong Ge, Jun Zhang
papers.evidence: 扩散采样中扰动传播的理论及可控生成
papers.tldr: 扩散模型采样常被修改以控制生成或加速，但轨迹扰动如何传播到输出尚不清楚。本文结合动力系统分析与信息论，提出扰动传播理论框架，用KL散度定义路径代价，并推导响应恒等式。实验在相同路径代价下干预预训练模型，发现输出敏感度随采样阶段和空间频率呈现不同模式。该框架还能诊断缓存加速中的误差区间，为理解和改进采样修改提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in generative modeling, with their sampling procedures routinely modified to control generation and improve efficiency. These modifications introduce perturbations along the sampling trajectory, raising a central question: how do such perturbations affect generated output? To address this question, we develop a theoretical framework to investigate perturbation propagation, combining dynamical analysis of the sampling process with an information-theoretic characterization of output responses. Within this framework, we quantify perturbation strength using the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence between perturbed and reference trajectory distributions, termed as path cost, which is shown to bound, but do not determine, changes in the output distribution. Building on this analysis, we derive a response identity that connects the propagation and accumulation of local perturbations with the information captured by a selected feature mean, explaining why changes in the output distribution can remain undetected by its first-order response. We test our theoretical analysis through controlled interventions at equal path cost in pretrained diffusion models, revealing distinct patterns of output sensitivity across sampling stages and spatial frequencies. To assess whether our framework can diagnose perturbations arising from practical approximations, we apply it to cache-based acceleration and show that our propagation analysis reliably identifies sampling intervals where caching causes larger image errors.

papers.title_en: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Wuzhe Xu, Zhaiming Shen, Yulong Lu, Wenjing Liao, Rongjie Lai
papers.evidence: 面向扩散模型的上下文评分算子学习
papers.tldr: 扩散模型多针对固定条件或单一分布训练，难以仅凭少量样本适应未见分布。本文提出上下文评分算子学习框架，把每个目标分布视为元分布中的任务，由推理时上下文集指定，并学习从上下文样本、噪声查询点和扩散时间到任务评分的Transformer映射。理论上该评分可写成高斯核条件均值，经验Nadaraya-Watson近似可由构造Transformer精确表示，并给出泛化误差界。在Navier-Stokes、ERA5、QuickDraw、Food-101上，简单任务族表现良好，复杂度升高时性能下降。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion models typically learn the generative dynamics of a single target distribution or a family of distributions indexed by conditioning variables fixed during training. This limits their ability to adapt to a previously unseen distribution from only a small set of examples. We introduce an in-context solution operator learning framework for diffusion models, in which each target distribution is treated as a task drawn from a meta-distribution and is specified at inference time by an empirical context set. Our method learns an in-context score operator that maps the context samples, a noisy query point, and the diffusion time to the task-dependent score, enabling reverse-diffusion sampling on unseen tasks without retraining or parameter updates. A key observation is that the task-dependent score admits a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation. Its empirical Nadaraya--Watson approximation can be represented exactly by a model in our constructed transformer class, providing a principled foundation for the proposed query-dependent attention architecture. The operator is trained through amortized denoising score matching across task distributions. We establish generalization-error bounds that quantify the effects of the context size, the numbers of training tasks and within-task samples, model complexity, and intrinsic and ambient dimensions. Numerically, we evaluate the method on a range of scientific and visual datasets, including Navier-Stokes, ERA5 climate data, QuickDraw sketches, and Food-101. The results show that the proposed method performs well on relatively simple task families, while its performance degrades as task complexity increases, thereby illustrating both the promise and the limitations of in-context learning for diffusion models.
